instruction:
Work from a CalculiX cantilever beam template `/home/user/Desktop/uniform_beam.inp` (one B31 element, 10x10 mm RECT section, clamped at node 1, tip load FY=-100 N at node 2). Run `ccx --version` or invoke the installed `ccx` binary from a terminal; use `/usr/bin/ccx` for the solve.

Rebuild the model as a stepped beam with a 10-element mesh and generate `/home/user/Desktop/solution.inp`:
- 11 nodes: node i at coordinates `(10*(i-1), 0, 0)` for i = 1..11 (so node 1 at x=0 and node 11 at x=100)
- 10 B31 elements: element e connects nodes `e` and `e+1`, for e = 1..10
- Sections by region: elements 1-5 use a `10x10 mm` RECT section; elements 6-10 use a `6x6 mm` RECT section, assigned through element sets of your choice
- Keep the material (E=210000, nu=0.3), the clamped boundary at node 1 (dofs 1-6) and the tip load FY=-100 N at node 11 unchanged

Submit the job with `ccx` and produce `/home/user/Desktop/solution.dat` (in CalculiX, results reach `.dat` through `*Node Print`, which requires an explicit node set; the template defines `All_Nodes` and shows a working print card)

Post-process the results and write `/home/user/Desktop/summary.txt` in this exact format (two comma-separated numbers): `step_uy, tip_uy`
- `step_uy`: vertical displacement UY of node 6 (the first node of the thin segment)
- `tip_uy`: vertical displacement UY of node 11 (the loaded tip)
